35.s:
athocyate samastānāṃ śāstrāṇāmiha melanam /
iha tāvatsama sto'yaṃ vyavahāraḥ purātanaḥ // 1
35.d:
अथोच्यते समस्तानां शास्त्राणामिह मेलनम् ।
इह तावत्सम स्तोऽयं व्यवहारः पुरातनः ॥ 1
35.m:
Now is explained the harmonization of all scriptures here [in this system].
First of all, here, all this ancient conventional practice

35.s:
prasiddhimanusandhāya saiva cāgama ucyate /
anvayavyatirekau hi prasiddherupajīvakau // 2
35.d:
प्रसिद्धिमनुसन्धाय सैव चागम उच्यते ।
अन्वयव्यतिरेकौ हि प्रसिद्धेरुपजीवकौ ॥ 2
35.m:
is based on established consensus; and that very [consensus] is called scriptural tradition.
For positive and negative concomitance indeed depend upon established consensus.

35.s:
svāyattatve tayorvyaktipūge kiṃ syāttayorgatiḥ /
pratyakṣamapi netrātmadīpārthādiviśeṣajam // 3
35.d:
स्वायत्तत्वे तयोर्व्यक्तिपूगे किं स्यात्तयोर्गतिः ।
प्रत्यक्षमपि नेत्रात्मदीपार्थादिविशेषजम् ॥ 3
35.m:
If those two were self-dependent, what would be their scope within an assemblage of particulars?
Even perception, produced from specific factors such as the eye, oneself, a lamp, and the object,

35.s:
apekṣate tatra mūle prasiddhiṃ tāṃ tathātmikām /
abhitaḥsaṃvṛte jāta ekākī kṣudhitaḥ śiśuḥ // 4
35.d:
अपेक्षते तत्र मूले प्रसिद्धिं तां तथात्मिकाम् ।
अभितःसंवृते जात एकाकी क्षुधितः शिशुः ॥ 4
35.m:
relies at its root on that established consensus having that nature.
A hungry child born alone in an enclosed space,

35.s:
kiṃ karotu kimādattāṃ kena paśyatu kiṃ vrajet /
nanu vastuśatākīrṇe sthāne'pyasya yadeva hi // 5
35.d:
किं करोतु किमादत्तां केन पश्यतु किं व्रजेत् ।
ननु वस्तुशताकीर्णे स्थानेऽप्यस्य यदेव हि ॥ 5
35.m:
what could it do? What could it grasp? With what could it see? Whither could it go?
Is it not the case that even in a place strewn with hundreds of objects, whatever it is that,

35.s:
paśyato jighrato vāpi spṛśataḥ saṃprasīdati /
cetastadevādāya drāk so'nvayavyatirekabhāk // 6
35.d:
पश्यतो जिघ्रतो वापि स्पृशतः संप्रसीदति ।
चेतस्तदेवादाय द्राक् सोऽन्वयव्यतिरेकभाक् ॥ 6
35.m:
as he sees, smells, or touches it, pleases his mind,
grasping instantly that very thing, he possesses positive and negative concomitance?

35.s:
hanta cetaḥprasādo'pi yo'sāvarthaviśeṣagaḥ /
so'pi prāgvāsanārūpavimarśaparikalpitaḥ // 7
35.d:
हन्त चेतःप्रसादोऽपि योऽसावर्थविशेषगः ।
सोऽपि प्राग्वासनारूपविमर्शपरिकल्पितः ॥ 7
35.m:
Ah! Even that mental satisfaction which pertains to a particular object
is also projected by a reflective awareness in the form of latent traces from before.

35.s:
na pratyakṣānumānādibāhyamānaprasādajaḥ /
prāgvāsanopajīvyetat pratibhāmātrameva na // 8
35.d:
न प्रत्यक्षानुमानादिबाह्यमानप्रसादजः ।
प्राग्वासनोपजीव्येतत् प्रतिभामात्रमेव न ॥ 8
35.m:
It is not produced by the favor of an external means of knowledge such as perception or inference.
This depends on previous latent traces; it is not mere intuitive flash.

35.s:
na mṛdabhyavahārecchā puṃso bālasya jāyate /
prāgvāsanopajīvī cedvimarśaḥ sā ca vāsanā // 9
35.d:
न मृदभ्यवहारेच्छा पुंसो बालस्य जायते ।
प्राग्वासनोपजीवी चेद्विमर्शः सा च वासना ॥ 9
35.m:
A child has no desire to eat mud.
If reflective awareness depends on latent traces from before, and if that latent trace

35.s:
prācyā cedāgatā seyaṃ prasiddhiḥ paurvakālikī /
naca cetaḥprasattyaiva sarvo vyavahṛtikramaḥ // 10
35.d:
प्राच्या चेदागता सेयं प्रसिद्धिः पौर्वकालिकी ।
नच चेतःप्रसत्त्यैव सर्वो व्यवहृतिक्रमः ॥ 10
35.m:
comes from earlier, that is this established consensus of past time;
and the entire course of conventional behavior is not [governed] solely by mental satisfaction.

35.s:
mūlaṃ prasiddhistanmānaṃ sarvatraiveti gṛhyatām /
pūrvapūrvopajīvitvamārgaṇe sā kvacitsvayam // 11
35.d:
मूलं प्रसिद्धिस्तन्मानं सर्वत्रैवेति गृह्यताम् ।
पूर्वपूर्वोपजीवित्वमार्गणे सा क्वचित्स्वयम् ॥ 11
35.m:
Let it be grasped that established consensus is the root, the means of knowledge everywhere.
When inquiring into dependence on prior and prior [traces], it [must] somewhere spontaneously

35.s:
sarvajñarūpe hyekasminniḥśaṅkaṃ bhāsata purā /
vyavahāro hi naikatra samastaḥ ko'pi mātari // 12
35.d:
सर्वज्ञरूपे ह्येकस्मिन्निःशङ्कं भासत पुरा ।
व्यवहारो हि नैकत्र समस्तः कोऽपि मातरि ॥ 12
35.m:
shine forth without doubt in the beginning within a single omniscient one;
for convention as a whole does not exist together in any [ordinary] cogniser.

35.s:
tenāsarvajñapūrvatvamātreṇaiṣā na siddhyati /
bahusarvajñapūrvatve na mānaṃ cāsti kiṃcana // 13
35.d:
तेनासर्वज्ञपूर्वत्वमात्रेणैषा न सिद्ध्यति ।
बहुसर्वज्ञपूर्वत्वे न मानं चास्ति किंचन ॥ 13
35.m:
Therefore it is not established merely through being preceded by a non-omniscient one;
and there is no proof whatsoever for its being preceded by many omniscient ones.

35.s:
bhogāpavargataddhetuprasiddhiśataśobhitaḥ /
tadvimarśasvabhāvo'sau bhairavaḥ parameśvaraḥ // 14
35.d:
भोगापवर्गतद्धेतुप्रसिद्धिशतशोभितः ।
तद्विमर्शस्वभावोऽसौ भैरवः परमेश्वरः ॥ 14
35.m:
Adorned with hundreds of established consensus regarding enjoyment, liberation, and their causes,
possessing the nature of reflective awareness thereof, is Bhairava, the Supreme Lord.

35.s:
tataścāṃśāṃśikāyogātsā prasiddhiḥ paramparām /
śāstraṃ vāśritya vitatā lokānsaṃvyavahārayet // 15
35.d:
ततश्चांशांशिकायोगात्सा प्रसिद्धिः परम्पराम् ।
शास्त्रं वाश्रित्य वितता लोकान्संव्यवहारयेत् ॥ 15
35.m:
And from him, through connection with parts and sub-parts, that established consensus, having expanded
by relying on lineage or scripture, engages the worlds in conventional behavior.

35.s:
tayaivāśaiśavātsarve vyavahāradharājuṣaḥ /
santaḥ samupajīvanti śaivamevādyamāgamam // 16
35.d:
तयैवाशैशवात्सर्वे व्यवहारधराजुषः ।
सन्तः समुपजीवन्ति शैवमेवाद्यमागमम् ॥ 16
35.m:
By that very [tradition] alone, all people from childhood onward who dwell upon the earth of conventional practice,
being wise, depend upon the primal Śaiva scriptural tradition alone.

35.s:
apūrṇāstu pare tena na mokṣaphalabhāginaḥ /
upajīvanti yāvattu tāvattatphalabhāginaḥ // 17
35.d:
अपूर्णास्तु परे तेन न मोक्षफलभागिनः ।
उपजीवन्ति यावत्तु तावत्तत्फलभागिनः ॥ 17
35.m:
Others, however, being incomplete, do not share in the fruit of liberation through it;
but to the extent that they rely on it, to that extent they share in its fruits.

35.s:
bālyāpāye'pi yadbhoktumannameṣa pravartate /
tatprasiddhyaiva nādhyakṣānnānumānādasambhavāt // 18
35.d:
बाल्यापायेऽपि यद्भोक्तुमन्नमेष प्रवर्तते ।
तत्प्रसिद्ध्यैव नाध्यक्षान्नानुमानादसम्भवात् ॥ 18
35.m:
Even when childhood has passed, that one proceeds to eat food
only by established consensus, not by perception nor by inference, because of [their] impossibility.

35.s:
naca kāpyatra doṣāśāśaṅkāyāśca nivṛttitaḥ /
prasiddhiścāvigānotthā pratītiḥ śabdanātmikā // 19
35.d:
नच काप्यत्र दोषाशाशङ्कायाश्च निवृत्तितः ।
प्रसिद्धिश्चाविगानोत्था प्रतीतिः शब्दनात्मिका ॥ 19
35.m:
Nor is there any apprehension of error here, because suspicion has ceased;
and established consensus is an uncontradicted cognition consisting of articulation.

35.s:
mātuḥ svabhāvo yattasyāṃ śaṅkate naiṣa jātucit /
svakṛtatvavaśādeva sarvavitsa hi śaṅkaraḥ // 20
35.d:
मातुः स्वभावो यत्तस्यां शङ्कते नैष जातुचित् ।
स्वकृतत्ववशादेव सर्ववित्स हि शङ्करः ॥ 20
35.m:
Because it is the nature of the cogniser, he never doubts it;
for Śaṅkara is the all-knower solely by virtue of having made it himself.

35.s:
yāvattu śivatā nāsya tāvatsvātmānusāriṇīm /
tāvatīmeva tāmeṣa prasiddhiṃ nābhiśaṅkate // 21
35.d:
यावत्तु शिवता नास्य तावत्स्वात्मानुसारिणीम् ।
तावतीमेव तामेष प्रसिद्धिं नाभिशङ्कते ॥ 21
35.m:
As long as his Śivahood is not [realized], he does not doubt
just that much established consensus which conforms to his own self.

35.s:
anyasyāmabhiśaṅkī syādbhūyastāṃ bahu manyate /
evaṃ bhāviśivatvo'mūṃ prasiddhiṃ manyate dhruvam // 22
35.d:
अन्यस्यामभिशङ्की स्याद्भूयस्तां बहु मन्यते ।
एवं भाविशिवत्वोऽमूं प्रसिद्धिं मन्यते ध्रुवम् ॥ 22
35.m:
Regarding another [consensus] he might be doubtful, or esteem it highly;
thus, one destined for Śivahood certainly respects this established consensus.

35.s:
eka evāgamaścāyaṃ vibhunā sarvadarśinā /
darśito yaḥ pravṛtte ca nivṛtte ca pathi sthitaḥ // 23
35.d:
एक एवागमश्चायं विभुना सर्वदर्शिना ।
दर्शितो यः प्रवृत्ते च निवृत्ते च पथि स्थितः ॥ 23
35.m:
And this scriptural tradition is single alone, revealed by the all-seeing, all-pervading Lord,
which stands on both the path of worldly engagement and that of cessation.

35.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu pūrṇāpūrṇādibhedataḥ /
vicitreṣu phaleṣveka upāyaḥ śāmbhavāgamaḥ // 24
35.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु पूर्णापूर्णादिभेदतः ।
विचित्रेषु फलेष्वेक उपायः शाम्भवागमः ॥ 24
35.m:
Regarding virtue, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, diverse in their fruits
according to distinctions such as complete and incomplete, the Śāmbhava scriptural tradition is the single means.

35.s:
tasminviṣayavaiviktyādvicitraphaladāyini /
citropāyopadeśo'pi na virodhāvaho bhavet // 25
35.d:
तस्मिन्विषयवैविक्त्याद्विचित्रफलदायिनि ।
चित्रोपायोपदेशोऽपि न विरोधावहो भवेत् ॥ 25
35.m:
In that [tradition], which yields manifold fruits through differentiation of spheres,
even the teaching of manifold means would not entail any contradiction.

35.s:
laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ yogādi pāñcarātrakam /
bauddhārhatanyāyaśāstraṃ padārthakramatantraṇam // 26
35.d:
लौकिकं वैदिकं साङ्ख्यं योगादि पाञ्चरात्रकम् ।
बौद्धार्हतन्यायशास्त्रं पदार्थक्रमतन्त्रणम् ॥ 26
35.m:
The worldly, the Vedic, Sāṅkhya, Yoga and so on, Pāñcarātra,
the Buddhist, the Jaina, the Nyāya treatise, the systematic arrangement of the categories:

35.s:
siddhāntatantraśāktādi sarvaṃ brahmodbhavaṃ yataḥ /
śrīsvacchandādiṣu proktaṃ sadyojātādibhedataḥ // 27
35.d:
सिद्धान्ततन्त्रशाक्तादि सर्वं ब्रह्मोद्भवं यतः ।
श्रीस्वच्छन्दादिषु प्रोक्तं सद्योजातादिभेदतः ॥ 27
35.m:
Because everything—beginning with Siddhānta, Tantra, and Śākta—arises from Brahman,
as declared in the venerable Svacchanda and elsewhere, through the differentiation of Sadyojāta and the others. // 27

35.s:
yathaikatrāpi vedādau tattadāśramagāminaḥ /
saṃskārāntaramatrāpi tathā liṅgoddhṛtādikam // 28
35.d:
यथैकत्रापि वेदादौ तत्तदाश्रमगामिनः ।
संस्कारान्तरमत्रापि तथा लिङ्गोद्धृतादिकम् ॥ 28
35.m:
Just as even within a single [corpus] such as the Veda, those entering different stages of life
undergo a further rite of consecration, so here too with the removal of caste-marks and the rest. // 28

35.s:
yathāca tatra pūrvasminnāśrame nottarāśramāt /
phalameti tathā pāñcarātrādau na śivātmatām // 29
35.d:
यथाच तत्र पूर्वस्मिन्नाश्रमे नोत्तराश्रमात् ।
फलमेति तथा पाञ्चरात्रादौ न शिवात्मताम् ॥ 29
35.m:
And just as in that case one in an earlier stage of life does not obtain
the fruit of a higher stage of life, so in the Pāñcarātra and others one does not attain the state of Śiva. // 29

35.s:
eka evāgamastasmāttatra laukikaśāstrataḥ /
prabhṛtyāvaiṣṇavādbauddhācchaivātsarvaṃ hi niṣṭhitam // 30
35.d:
एक एवागमस्तस्मात्तत्र लौकिकशास्त्रतः ।
प्रभृत्यावैष्णवाद्बौद्धाच्छैवात्सर्वं हि निष्ठितम् ॥ 30
35.m:
Therefore, scripture is indeed one: starting from the mundane teaching,
up through the Vaiṣṇava, Buddhist, and Śaiva, all are established within it. // 30

35.s:
tasya yattat paraṃ prāpyaṃ dhāma tat trikaśabditam /
sarvāvibhedānucchedāt tadeva kulamucyate // 31
35.d:
तस्य यत्तत् परं प्राप्यं धाम तत् त्रिकशब्दितम् ।
सर्वाविभेदानुच्छेदात् तदेव कुलमुच्यते ॥ 31
35.m:
Its highest attainable abode is called Trika;
because of the non-severance of all without distinction, it is called Kula. // 31

35.s:
yathordhvādharatābhāksu dehāṅgeṣu vibhediṣu /
ekaṃ prāṇitamevaṃ syāt trikaṃ sarveṣu śāstrataḥ // 32
35.d:
यथोर्ध्वाधरताभाक्सु देहाङ्गेषु विभेदिषु ।
एकं प्राणितमेवं स्यात् त्रिकं सर्वेषु शास्त्रतः ॥ 32
35.m:
Just as in the differing limbs of the body, which possess higher and lower positions,
there is a single animation, so Trika is through all scriptures. // 32

35.s:
śrīmatkālīkule coktaṃ pañcasrotovivarjitam /
daśāṣṭādaśabhedasya sārametatprakīrtitam // 33
35.d:
श्रीमत्कालीकुले चोक्तं पञ्चस्रोतोविवर्जितम् ।
दशाष्टादशभेदस्य सारमेतत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 33
35.m:
And in the venerable Kālīkula it is said: free from the five currents,
this is proclaimed the essence of the eighteen-fold and ten-fold division. // 33

35.s:
puṣpe gandhastile tailaṃ dehe jīvo jale'mṛtam /
yathā tathaiva śāstrāṇāṃ kulamantaḥ pratiṣṭhitam // 34
35.d:
पुष्पे गन्धस्तिले तैलं देहे जीवो जलेऽमृतम् ।
यथा तथैव शास्त्राणां कुलमन्तः प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 34
35.m:
Just as fragrance in a flower, oil in sesame, life in the body, nectar in water,
even so is Kula situated within the scriptures. // 34

35.s:
tadeka evāgamo'yaṃ citraścitre'dhikāriṇi /
tathaiva sā prasiddhirhi svayūthyaparayūthyagā // 35
35.d:
तदेक एवागमोऽयं चित्रश्चित्रेऽधिकारिणि ।
तथैव सा प्रसिद्धिर्हि स्वयूथ्यपरयूथ्यगा ॥ 35
35.m:
Therefore, this scripture is one, yet diversified according to the varied competent person;
even so is that consensus recognized among members of one's own group and other groups. // 35

35.s:
sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ pāñcarātraṃ vedāṃścaiva na nindayet /
yataḥ śivodbhavāḥ sarva iti svacchandaśāsane // 36
35.d:
सांख्यं योगं पाञ्चरात्रं वेदांश्चैव न निन्दयेत् ।
यतः शिवोद्भवाः सर्व इति स्वच्छन्दशासने ॥ 36
35.m:
One should not revile Sāṅkhya, Yoga, Pāñcarātra, or the Vedas,
because all arise from Śiva, as [stated] in the doctrine of the Svacchanda. // 36

35.s:
ekasmādāgamāccaite khaṇḍakhaṇḍā vyapoddhṛtāḥ /
loke syurāgamāstaiśca jano bhrāmyati mohitaḥ // 37
35.d:
एकस्मादागमाच्चैते खण्डखण्डा व्यपोद्धृताः ।
लोके स्युरागमास्तैश्च जनो भ्राम्यति मोहितः ॥ 37
35.m:
And from this single scripture, these fragments were extracted
to become scriptures in the world, and by them deluded people wander astray. // 37

35.s:
anekāgamapakṣe'pi vācyā viṣayabheditā /
avaśyamūrdhvādharatāsthityā prāmāṇyasiddhaye // 38
35.d:
अनेकागमपक्षेऽपि वाच्या विषयभेदिता ।
अवश्यमूर्ध्वाधरतास्थित्या प्रामाण्यसिद्धये ॥ 38
35.m:
Even on the view of manifold scriptures, a difference of scope must necessarily be affirmed
according to the hierarchy of higher and lower, in order to establish authoritativeness. // 38

35.s:
anyathā naiva kasyāpi prāmāṇyaṃ siddhyati dhruvam /
nityatvamavisaṃvāda iti no mānakāraṇam // 39
35.d:
अन्यथा नैव कस्यापि प्रामाण्यं सिद्ध्यति ध्रुवम् ।
नित्यत्वमविसंवाद इति नो मानकारणम् ॥ 39
35.m:
Otherwise, the authoritativeness of none whatsoever is firmly established;
eternality or non-contradiction is not the criterion of valid knowledge. // 39

35.s:
asminnaṃśe'pyamuṣyaiva prāmāṇyaṃ syāttathoditeḥ /
anyathāvyākṛtau kḷptāvasatyatve prarocane // 40
35.d:
अस्मिन्नंशेऽप्यमुष्यैव प्रामाण्यं स्यात्तथोदितेः ।
अन्यथाव्याकृतौ कॢप्तावसत्यत्वे प्ररोचने ॥ 40
35.m:
Even in this part, authoritativeness would belong to this [scripture] alone, because it is so stated;
if explained otherwise, it would be an arbitrary assumption, falsehood, [or mere] enticement. // 40

35.s:
atiprasaṅga sarvasyāpyāgamasyāpabādhakaḥ /
avaśyopetya ityasminmāna āgamanāmani // 41
35.d:
अतिप्रसङ्ग सर्वस्याप्यागमस्यापबाधकः ।
अवश्योपेत्य इत्यस्मिन्मान आगमनामनि ॥ 41
35.m:
An absurd consequence undermines all scripture;
with regard to this means of valid knowledge named 'scripture', it must necessarily be accepted. // 41

35.s:
avaśyopetyamevaitacchāstraniṣṭhānirūpaṇam /
pradhāne'ṅge kṛto yatnaḥ phalavānvastuto yataḥ // 42
35.d:
अवश्योपेत्यमेवैतच्छास्त्रनिष्ठानिरूपणम् ।
प्रधानेऽङ्गे कृतो यत्नः फलवान्वस्तुतो यतः ॥ 42
35.m:
This determination of the ultimate import of scripture must necessarily be accepted,
since effort made on the principal element is truly fruitful. // 42

35.s:
ato'smin yatnavān ko'pi bhavecchaṃbhupracoditaḥ /
tatra tatra ca śāstreṣu nyarūpyata maheśinā // 43
35.d:
अतोऽस्मिन् यत्नवान् कोऽपि भवेच्छंभुप्रचोदितः ।
तत्र तत्र च शास्त्रेषु न्यरूप्यत महेशिना ॥ 43
35.m:
Therefore, someone inspired by Śambhu might exert effort in this,
and it has been explained here and there in the scriptures by the Great Lord. // 43

35.s:
etāvatyadhikārī yaḥ sa durlabha iti sphuṭam /
itthaṃ śrīśambhunāthena mamoktaṃ śāstramelanam // 44
35.d:
एतावत्यधिकारी यः स दुर्लभ इति स्फुटम् ।
इत्थं श्रीशम्भुनाथेन ममोक्तं शास्त्रमेलनम् ॥ 44
35.m:
A person qualified to this extent is rare, clearly;
thus was the integration of the scriptures spoken to me by the venerable Śambhunātha. // 44

36.s:
āyātiratha śāstrasya kathyate'vasarāgatā /
śrīsiddhādivinirdiṣṭā gurubhiśca nirūpitā /
bhairavo bhairavī devī svacchando lākulo'ṇurāṭ // 1
36.d:
आयातिरथ शास्त्रस्य कथ्यतेऽवसरागता ।
श्रीसिद्धादिविनिर्दिष्टा गुरुभिश्च निरूपिता ।
भैरवो भैरवी देवी स्वच्छन्दो लाकुलोऽणुराट् ॥ 1
36.m: Now the lineage of the teaching is described, having arrived in its proper turn, / as pointed out by the venerable Siddhā and others, and set forth by the gurus: / Bhairava, the goddess Bhairavī, Svacchanda, Lākula, the king of souls, // 1

36.s:
gahaneśo'bjajaḥ śakro guruḥ koṭyapakarṣataḥ /
navabhiḥ kramaśo'dhītaṃ navakoṭipravistaram // 2
36.d:
गहनेशोऽब्जजः शक्रो गुरुः कोट्यपकर्षतः ।
नवभिः क्रमशोऽधीतं नवकोटिप्रविस्तरम् ॥ 2
36.m: Gahaneśa, the lotus-born [Brahmā], Śakra, and the guru; by reducing a crore [at each stage], / it was studied successively by these nine in an extent of nine crores [of verses]. // 2

36.s:
etaistato guruḥ koṭimātrāt pādaṃ vitīrṇavān /
dakṣādibhya ubhau pādau saṃvartādibhya eva ca // 3
36.d:
एतैस्ततो गुरुः कोटिमात्रात् पादं वितीर्णवान् ।
दक्षादिभ्य उभौ पादौ संवर्तादिभ्य एव च ॥ 3
36.m: From these, then, the guru gave a fourth part out of just one crore / to Dakṣa and others, and two-fourths to Saṃvarta and others, // 3

36.s:
pādaṃ ca vāmanādibhyaḥ pādārdhaṃ bhārgavāya ca /
pādapādaṃ tu balaye pādapādastu yo'paraḥ // 4
36.d:
पादं च वामनादिभ्यः पादार्धं भार्गवाय च ।
पादपादं तु बलये पादपादस्तु योऽपरः ॥ 4
36.m: and a fourth to Vāmana and others, half of a fourth to the descendant of Bhṛgu, / a quarter of a fourth to Bali, and another quarter of a fourth, // 4

36.s:
siṃhāyārdhaṃ tataḥ śiṣṭāddvau bhāgau vinatābhuve /
pādaṃ vāsukināgāya khaṇḍāḥ saptadaśa tvamī // 5
36.d:
सिंहायार्धं ततः शिष्टाद्द्वौ भागौ विनताभुवे ।
पादं वासुकिनागाय खण्डाः सप्तदश त्वमी ॥ 5
36.m: half [of that] to the lion, then from the remainder two shares to the son of Vinatā [Garuḍa], / a fourth to the serpent Vāsuki—these are the seventeen portions. // 5

36.s:
svargādardhaṃ rāvaṇo'tha jahre rāmo'rdhamapyataḥ /
vibhīṣaṇamukhādāpa guruśiṣyavidhikramāt // 6
36.d:
स्वर्गादर्धं रावणोऽथ जह्रे रामोऽर्धमप्यतः ।
विभीषणमुखादाप गुरुशिष्यविधिक्रमात् ॥ 6
36.m: Then Rāvaṇa took half from heaven, and Rāma took half of that; / he obtained it from the mouth of Vibhīṣaṇa through the succession of the guru-disciple rule. // 6

36.s:
khaṇḍairekānnaviṃśatyā vibhaktaṃ tadabhūttataḥ /
khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ cāṣṭakhaṇḍaṃ proktapādādibhedataḥ // 7
36.d:
खण्डैरेकान्नविंशत्या विभक्तं तदभूत्ततः ।
खण्डं खण्डं चाष्टखण्डं प्रोक्तपादादिभेदतः ॥ 7
36.m: Then it was divided into nineteen portions; / and portion by portion it became an eight-part section, according to the division of the quarter-verses and so forth mentioned earlier: // 7

36.s:
pādo mūloddhārāvuttaravṛhaduttare tathā kalpaḥ /
sāṃhitakalpaskandāvanuttaraṃ vyāpakaṃ tridhā tisraḥ // 8
36.d:
पादो मूलोद्धारावुत्तरवृहदुत्तरे तथा कल्पः ।
सांहितकल्पस्कन्दावनुत्तरं व्यापकं त्रिधा तिस्रः ॥ 8
36.m: the quarter-verse, the two base extractions, the Uttara and Bṛhaduttara, and likewise the ritual manual, / the Saṃhitā manual and section, the unexcelled and the all-pervading in three forms; the three // 8

36.s:
devyo'tra nirūpyante kramaśo vistāriṇaiva rūpeṇa /
navame pade tu gaṇanā na kāciduktā vyavacchidāhīne // 9
36.d:
देव्योऽत्र निरूप्यन्ते क्रमशो विस्तारिणैव रूपेण ।
नवमे पदे तु गणना न काचिदुक्ता व्यवच्छिदाहीने ॥ 9
36.m: goddesses are set forth here in sequence in an expanded form, / but in the ninth quarter no enumeration whatsoever is stated, as it is free from distinctions. // 9

36.s:
rāmācca lakṣmaṇastasmāt siddhāstebhyo'pi dānavāḥ /
guhyakāśca tatastebhyo yogino nṛvarāstataḥ // 10
36.d:
रामाच्च लक्ष्मणस्तस्मात् सिद्धास्तेभ्योऽपि दानवाः ।
गुह्यकाश्च ततस्तेभ्यो योगिनो नृवरास्ततः ॥ 10
36.m: And from Rāma [it went to] Lakṣmaṇa, from him to the Siddhās, from them to the Dānavas / and Guhyakas, then from them to the Yogins, and from them to the best of men. // 10

36.s:
teṣāṃ krameṇa tanmadhye bhraṣṭaṃ kālāntarādyadā /
tadā śrīkaṇṭhanāthājñāvaśāt siddhā avātaram // 11
36.d:
तेषां क्रमेण तन्मध्ये भ्रष्टं कालान्तराद्यदा ।
तदा श्रीकण्ठनाथाज्ञावशात् सिद्धा अवातरम् ॥ 11
36.m: When, in the course of time, it was lost in their midst, / then, by the command of the lord Śrīkaṇṭha, the Siddhās descended: // 11

36.s:
tryambakāmardakābhikhyaśrīnāthā advaye dvaye /
dvayādvaye ca nipuṇāḥ krameṇa śivaśāsane // 12
36.d:
त्र्यम्बकामर्दकाभिख्यश्रीनाथा अद्वये द्वये ।
द्वयाद्वये च निपुणाः क्रमेण शिवशासने ॥ 12
36.m: the venerable lords named Tryambaka, Āmardaka, and Śrīnātha, skilled / in non-duality, duality, and qualified non-duality respectively, in the Śaiva teaching. // 12

36.s:
ādyasya cānvayo jajñe dvitīyo duhitṛkramāt /
sa cārdhatryambakābhikhyaḥ saṃtānaḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ // 13
36.d:
आद्यस्य चान्वयो जज्ञे द्वितीयो दुहितृक्रमात् ।
स चार्धत्र्यम्बकाभिख्यः संतानः सुप्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 13
36.m: And of the first, a second lineage arose through his daughter; / that well-established transmission is known as the Half-Tryambaka [tradition]. // 13

36.s:
ataścārdhacatasro'tra maṭhikāḥ saṃtatikramāt /
śiṣyapraśiṣyairvistīrṇāḥ śataśākhaṃ vyavasthitaiḥ // 14
36.d:
अतश्चार्धचतस्रोऽत्र मठिकाः संततिक्रमात् ।
शिष्यप्रशिष्यैर्विस्तीर्णाः शतशाखं व्यवस्थितैः ॥ 14
36.m: Hence there are here three and a half monasteries, by succession of transmission, / expanded by disciples and grand-disciples settled in a hundred branches. // 14

36.s:
adhyuṣṭasaṃtatisrotaḥsārabhūtarasāhṛtim /
vidhāya tantrāloko'yaṃ syandate sakalānrasān // 15
uktāyātirupādeyabhāvo nirṇīyate'dhunā /
36.d:
अध्युष्टसंततिस्रोतःसारभूतरसाहृतिम् ।
विधाय तन्त्रालोकोऽयं स्यन्दते सकलान्रसान् ॥ 15
उक्तायातिरुपादेयभावो निर्णीयतेऽधुना ।
36.m:
Having extracted the essential aesthetic flavor from the current of the three and a half lineages, / this Tantrāloka pours forth all aesthetic flavors. // 15
The lineage has been stated; what is to be accepted is now determined.

37.s:
uktanītyaiva sarvatra vyavahāre pravartite /
prasiddhāvupajīvyāyāmavaśyagrāhya āgamaḥ // 1
37.d:
उक्तनीत्यैव सर्वत्र व्यवहारे प्रवर्तिते ।
प्रसिद्धावुपजीव्यायामवश्यग्राह्य आगमः ॥ 1
37.m: When ordinary worldly practice is conducted everywhere according to the stated method, / scripture must necessarily be accepted when relying on conventional consensus. // 1

37.s:
yathā laukikadṛṣṭyānyaphalabhāk tatprasiddhitaḥ /
samyagvyavaharaṃstadvacchivabhāk tatprasiddhitaḥ // 2
37.d:
यथा लौकिकदृष्ट्यान्यफलभाक् तत्प्रसिद्धितः ।
सम्यग्व्यवहरंस्तद्वच्छिवभाक् तत्प्रसिद्धितः ॥ 2
37.m: Just as one acting correctly from a mundane perspective attains another fruit through that consensus, / so one attains Śiva through that consensus. // 2

37.s:
tadavaśyagrahītavye śāstre svāṃśopadeśini /
manākphale'bhyupādeyatamaṃ tadviparītakam // 3
37.d:
तदवश्यग्रहीतव्ये शास्त्रे स्वांशोपदेशिनि ।
मनाक्फलेऽभ्युपादेयतमं तद्विपरीतकम् ॥ 3
37.m: Therefore, when scripture teaching a part of itself must necessarily be accepted, / that which produces minimal fruit is surpassed by its opposite as the most worthy of acceptance. // 3

37.s:
yathā khageśvarībhāvaniḥśaṅkatvādviṣaṃ vrajet /
kṣayaṃ karmasthitistadvadaśaṅkādbhairavatvataḥ // 4
37.d:
यथा खगेश्वरीभावनिःशङ्कत्वाद्विषं व्रजेत् ।
क्षयं कर्मस्थितिस्तद्वदशङ्काद्भैरवत्वतः ॥ 4
37.m: Just as poison is destroyed through the fearless state of the Queen of birds [Garuḍa], / so the persistence of karma is destroyed through the fearless state of Bhairava. // 4

37.s:
yadārṣe pātahetūktaṃ tadasminvāmaśāsane /
āśusiddhyai yataḥ sarvamārṣaṃ māyodarasthitam // 5
37.d:
यदार्षे पातहेतूक्तं तदस्मिन्वामशासने ।
आशुसिद्ध्यै यतः सर्वमार्षं मायोदरस्थितम् ॥ 5
37.m: What is declared in the Vedic tradition to be a cause of downfall serves, in this left-hand doctrine, / for rapid accomplishment, because all Vedic tradition resides within the belly of Māyā. // 5

37.s:
tacca yatsarvasarvajñadṛṣṭaṃ taccāpi kiṃ bhavet /
yadaśeṣopadeśena sūyate'nuttaraṃ phalam // 6
37.d:
तच्च यत्सर्वसर्वज्ञदृष्टं तच्चापि किं भवेत् ।
यदशेषोपदेशेन सूयतेऽनुत्तरं फलम् ॥ 6
37.m: And that which is seen by the all-knower of all—what can that be? / It is that which, through complete teaching, produces the unexcelled fruit. // 6

37.s:
yathādharādharaproktavastutattvānuvādataḥ /
uttaraṃ kathitaṃ saṃvitsiddhaṃ taddhi tathā bhavet // 7
37.d:
यथाधराधरप्रोक्तवस्तुतत्त्वानुवादतः ।
उत्तरं कथितं संवित्सिद्धं तद्धि तथा भवेत् ॥ 7
37.m: Just as, from the restatement of the real entities taught in lower and lower [scriptures], / the higher is proclaimed, that is indeed established by consciousness in that way. // 7

37.s:
yaduktādhikasaṃvittisiddhavastunirūpaṇāt /
apūrṇasarvavitproktirjñāyate'dharaśāsane // 8
37.d:
यदुक्ताधिकसंवित्तिसिद्धवस्तुनिरूपणात् ।
अपूर्णसर्ववित्प्रोक्तिर्ज्ञायतेऽधरशासने ॥ 8
37.m: Because of the exposition of realities established in higher consciousness than that, / the lower teaching is known to be the utterance of an incomplete knower of all. // 8

37.s:
ūrdhvaśāsanavastvaṃśe dṛṣṭvāpica samujjhite /
adhaḥ śāstreṣu māyātvaṃ lakṣyate sargarakṣaṇāt // 9
37.d:
ऊर्ध्वशासनवस्त्वंशे दृष्ट्वापिच समुज्झिते ।
अधः शास्त्रेषु मायात्वं लक्ष्यते सर्गरक्षणात् ॥ 9
37.m: And when an element of reality from the higher teaching is seen yet abandoned, / the nature of illusion is perceived in the lower scriptures, because of preserving creation. // 9

37.s:
śrīmadānandaśāstrādau proktaṃ ca parameśinā /
ṛṣivākyaṃ bahukleśamadhruvālpaphalaṃ mitam // 10
37.d:
श्रीमदानन्दशास्त्रादौ प्रोक्तं च परमेशिना ।
ऋषिवाक्यं बहुक्लेशमध्रुवाल्पफलं मितम् ॥ 10
37.m: And in the venerable Ānandaśāstra and elsewhere it is said by the Supreme Lord: / 'The word of the sages involves much affliction, has uncertain and meager fruit, and is limited. // 10

37.s:
naiva pramāṇayedvidvān śaivamevāgamaṃ śrayet /
tadārṣe pātahetūktaṃ tadasmin vāmaśāsane // 11
37.d:
नैव प्रमाणयेद्विद्वान् शैवमेवागमं श्रयेत् ।
तदार्षे पातहेतूक्तं तदस्मिन् वामशासने ॥ 11
37.m: The wise person should never accept it as authoritative; he should resort only to the Śaiva scripture.' / Therefore, what was stated in the Vedic tradition to be a cause of downfall, that [leads to accomplishment] in this left-hand doctrine. // 11

37.s:
āśusiddhyai yataḥ sarvamārṣaṃ māyodarasthitam /
yathā khageśvarībhāvaniḥśaṅkatvādviṣaṃ vrajet // 12
37.d:
आशुसिद्ध्यै यतः सर्वमार्षं मायोदरस्थितम् ।
यथा खगेश्वरीभावनिःशङ्कत्वाद्विषं व्रजेत् ॥ 12
37.m: For rapid spiritual accomplishment, since all that derives from the sages resides within the womb of māyā. / Just as poison is dispelled because of fearlessness arising from the condition of being the mistress of the skies,

37.s:
kṣayaṃ karmasthitistadvadaśaṅkādbhairavatvataḥ /
ajñatvānupadeṣṭṛtvasaṃdaṣṭe'dharaśāsane // 13
37.d:
क्षयं कर्मस्थितिस्तद्वदशङ्काद्भैरवत्वतः ।
अज्ञत्वानुपदेष्टृत्वसंदष्टेऽधरशासने ॥ 13
37.m: So the persistence of karma is destroyed by the condition of Bhairava that is free of doubt. / When the lower teaching is afflicted by ignorance and lack of genuine instruction,

37.s:
etadviparyayādgrāhyamavaśyaṃ śivaśāsanam /
dvāvāptau tatra ca śrīmacchrīkaṇṭhalakuleśvarau // 14
37.d:
एतद्विपर्ययाद्ग्राह्यमवश्यं शिवशासनम् ।
द्वावाप्तौ तत्र च श्रीमच्छ्रीकण्ठलकुलेश्वरौ ॥ 14
37.m: Through its opposite, the teaching of Śiva must necessarily be accepted. / And therein are two authoritative masters: the venerable Śrīkaṇṭha and Lakuleśvara.

37.s:
dvipravāhamidaṃ śāstraṃ mamyaṅniḥśreyasapradam /
prācyasya tu yathābhīṣṭabhogadatvamapi sthitam // 15
37.d:
द्विप्रवाहमिदं शास्त्रं मम्यङ्निःश्रेयसप्रदम् ।
प्राच्यस्य तु यथाभीष्टभोगदत्वमपि स्थितम् ॥ 15
37.m: This scripture of two streams truly bestows the highest good; / moreover, the capacity of the former to bestow desired enjoyments is also established.

37.s:
tacca pañcavidhaṃ proktaṃ śaktivaicitryacitritam /
pañcasrota iti proktaṃ śrīmacchrīkaṇṭhaśāsanam // 16
37.d:
तच्च पञ्चविधं प्रोक्तं शक्तिवैचित्र्यचित्रितम् ।
पञ्चस्रोत इति प्रोक्तं श्रीमच्छ्रीकण्ठशासनम् ॥ 16
37.m: And that is declared to be fivefold, variegated by the diversity of powers; / the teaching of the venerable Śrīkaṇṭha is called the five streams.

37.s:
daśāṣṭādaśadhā srotaḥpañcakaṃ yattato'pyalam /
utkṛṣṭaṃ bhairavābhikhyaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭivibheditam // 17
37.d:
दशाष्टादशधा स्रोतःपञ्चकं यत्ततोऽप्यलम् ।
उत्कृष्टं भैरवाभिख्यं चतुःषष्टिविभेदितम् ॥ 17
37.m: That quintet of streams is divided ten- and eighteen-fold; far superior even to that / is what is named Bhairava, divided into sixty-four [Tantras].

37.s:
śrīmadānandaśāstrādau proktaṃ bhagavatā kila /
samūhaḥ pīṭhametacca dvidhā dakṣiṇavāmataḥ // 18
37.d:
श्रीमदानन्दशास्त्रादौ प्रोक्तं भगवता किल ।
समूहः पीठमेतच्च द्विधा दक्षिणवामतः ॥ 18
37.m: It is stated by the Lord in the venerable Ānandaśāstra and elsewhere: / a collection is a seat, and this is twofold, according to Dakṣiṇa and Vāma.

37.s:
mantro vidyeti tasmācca mudrāmaṇḍalagaṃ dvayam /
mananatrāṇadaṃ yattu mantrākhyaṃ tatra vidyayā // 19
37.d:
मन्त्रो विद्येति तस्माच्च मुद्रामण्डलगं द्वयम् ।
मननत्राणदं यत्तु मन्त्राख्यं तत्र विद्यया ॥ 19
37.m: From that arise the two based on mantra and vidyā, which belong to mudrā and maṇḍala. / Among these, that which gives reflective thought and protection is called mantra; through vidyā

37.s:
upodbalanamāpyāyaḥ sā hi vedyārthabhāsinī /
mantrapratikṛtirmudrā tadāpyāyanakārakam // 20
37.d:
उपोद्बलनमाप्यायः सा हि वेद्यार्थभासिनी ।
मन्त्रप्रतिकृतिर्मुद्रा तदाप्यायनकारकम् ॥ 20
37.m: Comes its strengthening and nourishment, for she illuminates the object to be known. / Mudrā is the replica of mantra; it brings about that nourishment.

37.s:
maṇḍalaṃ sāramuktaṃ hi maṇḍaśrutyā śivāhvayam /
evamanyonyasaṃbhedavṛtti pīṭhacatuṣṭayam // 21
37.d:
मण्डलं सारमुक्तं हि मण्डश्रुत्या शिवाह्वयम् ।
एवमन्योन्यसंभेदवृत्ति पीठचतुष्टयम् ॥ 21
37.m: The maṇḍala is declared to be the essence, designated as Śiva because of the word maṇḍa ['essence']. / In this way, there is a quartet of seats whose functioning involves mutual interpenetration.

37.s:
yatastasmādbhavetsarvaṃ pīṭhe pīṭhe'pi vastutaḥ /
pradhānatvāttasya tasya vastuno bhinnatā punaḥ // 22
37.d:
यतस्तस्माद्भवेत्सर्वं पीठे पीठेऽपि वस्तुतः ।
प्रधानत्वात्तस्य तस्य वस्तुनो भिन्नता पुनः ॥ 22
37.m: Because of this, in truth everything exists in each seat; / nevertheless, through the predominance of one or another entity, a distinction

37.s:
kathitā sādhakendrāṇāṃ tattadvastuprasiddhaye /
pratyekaṃ taccaturdhaivaṃ maṇḍalaṃ mudrikā tathā // 23
37.d:
कथिता साधकेन्द्राणां तत्तद्वस्तुप्रसिद्धये ।
प्रत्येकं तच्चतुर्धैवं मण्डलं मुद्रिका तथा ॥ 23
37.m: Has been taught for supreme adepts to achieve those respective entities. / Each is thus fourfold: the maṇḍala, likewise the mudrā,

37.s:
mantro vidyeti ca pīṭhamutkṛṣṭaṃ cottarottam /
vidyāpīṭhapradhānaṃ ca siddhayogīśvarīmatam // 24
37.d:
मन्त्रो विद्येति च पीठमुत्कृष्टं चोत्तरोत्तम् ।
विद्यापीठप्रधानं च सिद्धयोगीश्वरीमतम् ॥ 24
37.m: The mantra, and the vidyā: each successive seat being superior. / And the Siddhayogīśvarīmata has the vidyāpīṭha as its foremost part.

37.s:
tasyāpi paramaṃ sāraṃ mālinīvijayottaram /
uktaṃ śrīratnamālāyāmetacca parameśinā // 25
37.d:
तस्यापि परमं सारं मालिनीविजयोत्तरम् ।
उक्तं श्रीरत्नमालायामेतच्च परमेशिना ॥ 25
37.m: Its supreme essence, too, is the Mālinīvijayottara; / this has been proclaimed by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Ratnamālā:

37.s:
aśeṣatantrasāraṃ tu vāmadakṣiṇamāśritam /
ekatra militaṃ kaulaṃ śrīṣaḍardhakaśāsane // 26
37.d:
अशेषतन्त्रसारं तु वामदक्षिणमाश्रितम् ।
एकत्र मिलितं कौलं श्रीषडर्धकशासने ॥ 26
37.m: “The essence of all Tantras, which relies on Vāma and Dakṣiṇa, / has met together as Kaula in the teaching of the venerable Trika.

37.s:
siddhānte karma bahulaṃ malamāyādirūṣitam /
dakṣiṇaṃ raudrakarmāḍhyaṃ vāmaṃ siddhisamākulam // 27
37.d:
सिद्धान्ते कर्म बहुलं मलमायादिरूषितम् ।
दक्षिणं रौद्रकर्माढ्यं वामं सिद्धिसमाकुलम् ॥ 27
37.m: In the Siddhānta there is abundant ritual action, stained by impurity, māyā, and the rest; / Dakṣiṇa is rich in terrifying acts; Vāma is crowded with spiritual accomplishments.

37.s:
svalpapuṇyaṃ bahukleśaṃ svapratītivivarjitam /
mokṣavidyāvihīnaṃ ca vinayaṃ tyaja dūrataḥ // 28
37.d:
स्वल्पपुण्यं बहुक्लेशं स्वप्रतीतिविवर्जितम् ।
मोक्षविद्याविहीनं च विनयं त्यज दूरतः ॥ 28
37.m: Abandon far away the [Buddhist] Vinaya: it yields little merit, involves great distress, lacks personal conviction, / and is devoid of the knowledge that brings liberation!”

37.s:
yasminkāle ca guruṇā nirvikalpaṃ prakāśitam /
muktastenaiva kālena yantraṃ tiṣṭhati kevalam // 29
37.d:
यस्मिन्काले च गुरुणा निर्विकल्पं प्रकाशितम् ।
मुक्तस्तेनैव कालेन यन्त्रं तिष्ठति केवलम् ॥ 29
37.m: And at the very moment when non-conceptual [awareness] is revealed by the guru, / at that very moment one is liberated: the body remains merely a mechanism.

37.s:
mayaitatsrotasāṃ rūpamanuttarapadāddhruvāt /
ārabhya vistareṇoktaṃ mālinīślokavārtike // 30
37.d:
मयैतत्स्रोतसां रूपमनुत्तरपदाद्ध्रुवात् ।
आरभ्य विस्तरेणोक्तं मालिनीश्लोकवार्तिके ॥ 30
37.m: The nature of these streams, beginning from the stable unexcelled plane, / has been explained by me in detail in the Mālinīślokavārttika.

37.s:
jijñāsustata evedamavadhārayituṃ kṣamaḥ /
vayaṃ tūktānuvacanamaphalaṃ nādriyāmahe // 31
37.d:
जिज्ञासुस्तत एवेदमवधारयितुं क्षमः ।
वयं तूक्तानुवचनमफलं नाद्रियामहे ॥ 31
37.m: One who desires to know can grasp this from that very work; / as for us, we do not care for the fruitless repetition of what has already been said.

37.s:
itthaṃ dadadanāyāsājjīvanmuktimahāphalam /
yathepsitamahābhogadātṛtvena vyavasthitam // 32
37.d:
इत्थं दददनायासाज्जीवन्मुक्तिमहाफलम् ।
यथेप्सितमहाभोगदातृत्वेन व्यवस्थितम् ॥ 32
37.m: Thus effortlessly granting the great fruit of liberation while living, / it is established as the giver of whatever great enjoyment is desired.

37.s:
ṣaḍardhasāraṃ sacchāstramupādeyamidaṃ sphuṭam /
ṣaṭtriṃśatā tattvabalena sūtā yadyapyanantā bhuvanāvalīyam /
brahmāṇḍamatyantamanoharaṃ tu vaicitryavarjaṃ nahi ramyabhāvaḥ // 33
37.d:
षडर्धसारं सच्छास्त्रमुपादेयमिदं स्फुटम् ।
षट्त्रिंशता तत्त्वबलेन सूता यद्यप्यनन्ता भुवनावलीयम् ।
ब्रह्माण्डमत्यन्तमनोहरं तु वैचित्र्यवर्जं नहि रम्यभावः ॥ 33
37.m: Clearly, this true scripture containing the essence of Trika is to be embraced. / Although this endless array of worlds was generated by the power of the thirty-six principles, / the cosmic egg is exceedingly charming, for beauty cannot exist without diversity.

37.s:
bhūrādisaptapurapūrṇatame'pi tasmin manye dvitīyabhuvanaṃ bhavanaṃ sukhasya /
kvānyatra citragatisūryaśaśāṅkaśobhirātrindivaprasarabhogavibhāgabhūṣā // 34
37.d:
भूरादिसप्तपुरपूर्णतमेऽपि तस्मिन् मन्ये द्वितीयभुवनं भवनं सुखस्य ।
क्वान्यत्र चित्रगतिसूर्यशशाङ्कशोभिरात्रिन्दिवप्रसरभोगविभागभूषा ॥ 34
37.m: Even in that [egg] replete with the seven realms beginning with earth, I consider the second world the abode of happiness; / where else is found that ornament dividing the experience of day and night, radiant with the sun and moon of wondrous course?

37.s:
tatrāpica tridivabhogamahārghavarṣadvīpāntarādadhikameva kumārikāhvam /
yatrādharādharapadātparamaṃ śivāntamāroḍhumapyadhikṛtiḥ kṛtināmanarghā // 35
37.d:
तत्रापिच त्रिदिवभोगमहार्घवर्षद्वीपान्तरादधिकमेव कुमारिकाह्वम् ।
यत्राधराधरपदात्परमं शिवान्तमारोढुमप्यधिकृतिः कृतिनामनर्घा ॥ 35
37.m: Even there, superior indeed to other continents and regions of heavenly enjoyment is that named Kumārikā, / where accomplished persons possess the priceless qualification to ascend from the lowest plane up to the supreme Śiva.

37.s:
prākkarmabhogipaśutocitabhogabhājā kiṃ janmanā nanu sukhaikapade'pi dhāmni /
sarvo hi bhāvini paraṃ paritoṣameti saṃbhāvite natu nimeṣiṇi vartamāne // 36
37.d:
प्राक्कर्मभोगिपशुतोचितभोगभाजा किं जन्मना ननु सुखैकपदेऽपि धाम्नि ।
सर्वो हि भाविनि परं परितोषमेति संभाविते नतु निमेषिणि वर्तमाने ॥ 36
37.m: Indeed, what is the use of a birth enjoying the pleasures appropriate to bound souls who merely experience past karma, even in a station that is the sole abode of happiness? / For everyone finds supreme satisfaction only in a prospective future, not in a fleeting present.

37.s:
kanyāhvaye'pi bhuvane'tra paraṃ mahīyān deśaḥ sa yatra kila śāstravarāṇi cakṣuḥ /
jātyandhasadmani na janma na ko'bhinindedbhinnāñjanāyitaravipramukhaprakāśe // 37
37.d:
कन्याह्वयेऽपि भुवनेऽत्र परं महीयान् देशः स यत्र किल शास्त्रवराणि चक्षुः ।
जात्यन्धसद्मनि न जन्म न कोऽभिनिन्देद्भिन्नाञ्जनायितरविप्रमुखप्रकाशे ॥ 37
37.m: Even in this realm called Kanyā, that country is truly preeminent where the best scriptures serve as eyes; / who would not censure a birth in the home of one blind from birth, where the light headed by the sun acts like dark collyrium?

37.s:
niḥśeṣaśāstrasadanaṃ kila madhyadeśastasminnajāyata guṇābhyadhiko dvijanmā /
ko'pyatrigupta iti nāmaniruktagotraḥ śāstrābdhicarvaṇakalodyadagastyagotraḥ // 38
37.d:
निःशेषशास्त्रसदनं किल मध्यदेशस्तस्मिन्नजायत गुणाभ्यधिको द्विजन्मा ।
कोऽप्यत्रिगुप्त इति नामनिरुक्तगोत्रः शास्त्राब्धिचर्वणकलोद्यदगस्त्यगोत्रः ॥ 38
37.m: The Middle Country (Madhyadeśa) is indeed the abode of all scriptures; in it was born a twice-born man of superior virtues, / a certain Atrigupta whose lineage-name was explained by his name, belonging to the lineage of Agastya, adept in the art of tasting the ocean of scriptures.

37.s:
tamatha lalitādityo rājā nijaṃ puramānayat praṇayarabhasāt kaśmīrākhyaṃ himālayamūrdhagam /
adhivasati yadgaurīkāntaḥ karairvijayādibhiryugapadakhilaṃ bhogāsāraṃ rasāt paricarcitum // 39
37.d:
तमथ ललितादित्यो राजा निजं पुरमानयत् प्रणयरभसात् कश्मीराख्यं हिमालयमूर्धगम् ।
अधिवसति यद्गौरीकान्तः करैर्विजयादिभिर्युगपदखिलं भोगासारं रसात् परिचर्चितुम् ॥ 39
37.m: King Lalitāditya then brought him out of intense affection to his own city called Kashmir, situated on the crest of the Himālaya, / which the Lord of Gaurī inhabits to savor with delight all at once the deluge of enjoyment through his rays, Vijaya and the rest.

37.s:
sthāne sthāne munibhirakhilaiścakrire yannivāsā yaccādhyāste pratipadamidaṃ sa svayaṃ candracūḍaḥ /
tanmanye'haṃ samabhilaṣitāśeṣasiddhernasiddhyai kaśmīrebhyaḥ paramatha puraṃ pūrṇavṛtterna tuṣṭyai // 40
37.d:
स्थाने स्थाने मुनिभिरखिलैश्चक्रिरे यन्निवासा यच्चाध्यास्ते प्रतिपदमिदं स स्वयं चन्द्रचूडः ।
तन्मन्येऽहं समभिलषिताशेषसिद्धेर्नसिद्ध्यै कश्मीरेभ्यः परमथ पुरं पूर्णवृत्तेर्न तुष्ट्यै ॥ 40
37.m: Where dwellings were made in place after place by all the sages, and which the Moon-Crested Lord himself inhabits at every step: / hence I think that for accomplishing all desired spiritual accomplishments there is no city beyond Kashmir, nor for the satisfaction of complete abundance.

37.s:
yatra svayaṃ śāradacandraśubhrā śrīśāradeti prathitā janeṣu /
śāṇḍilyasevārasasuprasannā sarvaṃ janaṃ svairvibhavairyunakti // 41
37.d:
यत्र स्वयं शारदचन्द्रशुभ्रा श्रीशारदेति प्रथिता जनेषु ।
शाण्डिल्यसेवारससुप्रसन्ना सर्वं जनं स्वैर्विभवैर्युनक्ति ॥ 41
37.m: Where she who is bright like the autumn moon, renowned among people as the venerable Śāradā, / highly pleased by the nectar of devotion from Śāṇḍilya, unites all people with her own glories;

37.s:
nāraṅgāruṇakānti pāṇḍuvikacadballāvadātacchavi prodbhinnāmalamātuluṅgakanakacchāyābhirāmaprabham /
kerīkuntalakandalīpratikṛtiśyāmaprabhābhāsvaraṃ yasmiñśakticatuṣṭayojjvalamalaṃ madyaṃ mahābhairavam // 42
37.d:
नारङ्गारुणकान्ति पाण्डुविकचद्बल्लावदातच्छवि प्रोद्भिन्नामलमातुलुङ्गकनकच्छायाभिरामप्रभम् ।
केरीकुन्तलकन्दलीप्रतिकृतिश्यामप्रभाभास्वरं यस्मिञ्शक्तिचतुष्टयोज्ज्वलमलं मद्यं महाभैरवम् ॥ 42
37.m: Where the great Bhairava wine shines brightly with its four powers: with the crimson radiance of an orange, with the pure hue of a pale blooming dballa flower, / with a lovely luster possessing the gold tint of an immaculate budding citron, and gleaming with a dark radiance imitating the sprout of a kerī palm;

37.s:
trinayanamahākopajvālāvilīna iha sthito madanaviśikhavrāto madyacchalena vijṛmbhate /
kathamitarathā rāgaṃ mohaṃ madaṃ madanajvaraṃ vidadhadaniśaṃ kāmātaṅkairvaśīkurute jagat // 43
37.d:
त्रिनयनमहाकोपज्वालाविलीन इह स्थितो मदनविशिखव्रातो मद्यच्छलेन विजृम्भते ।
कथमितरथा रागं मोहं मदं मदनज्वरं विदधदनिशं कामातङ्कैर्वशीकुरुते जगत् ॥ 43
37.m: Where the mass of Madana's arrows, melted in the flame of the great wrath of the Three-Eyed Lord, resides here and proliferates under the guise of wine; / how else, producing passion, bewilderment, intoxication, and the fever of lust, would it constantly subjugate the world with the distress of love?

37.s:
yatkāntānāṃ praṇayavacasi prauḍhimānaṃ vidatte yannirvighnaṃ nidhuvanavidhau sādhvasaṃ saṃdhunoti /
yasmin viśvāḥ kalitarucayo devatāścakracaryastanmārdvīkaṃ sapadi tanute yatra bhogāpabargau // 44
37.d:
यत्कान्तानां प्रणयवचसि प्रौढिमानं विदत्ते यन्निर्विघ्नं निधुवनविधौ साध्वसं संधुनोति ।
यस्मिन् विश्वाः कलितरुचयो देवताश्चक्रचर्यस्तन्मार्द्वीकं सपदि तनुते यत्र भोगापबर्गौ ॥ 44
37.m: Which produces bold maturity in the loving words of beloved women, which smoothly dispels hesitation in the rite of love-making, / in which all the goddesses delighting in circular rites have tasted pleasure: that very wine quickly brings about both enjoyment and liberation;

37.s:
udyadgaurāṅkuravikasitaiḥ śyāmaraktaiḥ palāśairantargāḍhāruṇarucilasatkesarālīvicitraiḥ /
ākīrṇā bhūḥ pratipadamasau yatra kāśmīrapuṣpaiḥ samyagdevītritayayajanodyānamāviṣkaroti // 45
37.d:
उद्यद्गौराङ्कुरविकसितैः श्यामरक्तैः पलाशैरन्तर्गाढारुणरुचिलसत्केसरालीविचित्रैः ।
आकीर्णा भूः प्रतिपदमसौ यत्र काश्मीरपुष्पैः सम्यग्देवीत्रितययजनोद्यानमाविष्करोति ॥ 45
37.m: Where, strewn at every step with saffron flowers variegated with dark-red petals unfurled with rising white sprouts, shining with rows of filaments glowing deep crimson within, / this land fully displays the garden for the worship of the triad of goddesses;

37.s:
sarvo lokaḥ kaviratha budho yatra śūro'pi vāgmī candroddyotā masṛṇagatayaḥ pauranāryaśca yatra /
yatrāṅgārojjvalavikasitānantasauṣumṇamārgagrastārkendurgaganavimalo yoginīnāṃ ca vargaḥ // 46
37.d:
सर्वो लोकः कविरथ बुधो यत्र शूरोऽपि वाग्मी चन्द्रोद्द्योता मसृणगतयः पौरनार्यश्च यत्र ।
यत्राङ्गारोज्ज्वलविकसितानन्तसौषुम्णमार्गग्रस्तार्केन्दुर्गगनविमलो योगिनीनां च वर्गः ॥ 46
37.m: Where everyone is a poet, a scholar, a hero, and an orator; where city women have the radiance of the moon and graceful gait; / and where the host of yoginīs is pure like the sky, having swallowed the sun and moon in the infinite path of the central channel glowing like burning embers.

37.s:
śrīmatparaṃ pravaranāma puraṃ ca tatra yannirmame pravarasena iti kṣitīśaḥ /
yaḥ svapratiṣṭhitamaheśvarapūjanānte vyomotpatannudasṛjatkila dhūpaghaṇṭām // 47
37.d:
श्रीमत्परं प्रवरनाम पुरं च तत्र यन्निर्ममे प्रवरसेन इति क्षितीशः ।
यः स्वप्रतिष्ठितमहेश्वरपूजनान्ते व्योमोत्पतन्नुदसृजत्किल धूपघण्टाम् ॥ 47
37.m: And there is that eminent city, Pravarapura by name, which king Pravarasena built; / who, having completed the worship of the Maheśvara installed by himself, cast up into the sky a censer-bell as he ascended to heaven.

37.s:
āndolanoditamanoharavīranādaiḥ sā cāsya tatsucaritaṃ prathayāṃbabhūva /
sadvṛttasāragurutaijasamūrtayo hi tyaktā api prabhuguṇānadhikaṃ dhvananti // 48
37.d:
आन्दोलनोदितमनोहरवीरनादैः सा चास्य तत्सुचरितं प्रथयांबभूव ।
सद्वृत्तसारगुरुतैजसमूर्तयो हि त्यक्ता अपि प्रभुगुणानधिकं ध्वनन्ति ॥ 48
37.m: And through charming, heroic sounds aroused by its swinging, it proclaimed his noble deeds; / for those formed of heavy, fiery matter and possessed of good conduct, even when cast off, sound forth the virtues of their master all the more.

37.s:
saṃpūrṇacandravimaladyutivīrakāntāgāḍhāṅgarāgaghanakuṅkumapiñjaraśrīḥ /
proddhūtavetasalatāsitacāmaraughairājyābhiṣekamaniśaṃ dadatī smarasya // 49
37.d:
संपूर्णचन्द्रविमलद्युतिवीरकान्तागाढाङ्गरागघनकुङ्कुमपिञ्जरश्रीः ।
प्रोद्धूतवेतसलतासितचामरौघैराज्याभिषेकमनिशं ददती स्मरस्य ॥ 49
37.m: Whose beauty was yellowish-red with thick saffron, like deep unguent of heroines with the spotless radiance of the full moon, / unceasingly giving a royal consecration to the God of Love by massed white chowries of tossed cane creepers;

37.s:
rodhaḥpratiṣṭhitamaheśvarasiddhaliṅgasvāyaṃbhuvārcanavilepanagandhapuṣpaiḥ /
āvarjyamānatanuvīcinimajjanaughavidhvastapāpmamunisiddhamanuṣyavandyā // 50
37.d:
रोधःप्रतिष्ठितमहेश्वरसिद्धलिङ्गस्वायंभुवार्चनविलेपनगन्धपुष्पैः ।
आवर्ज्यमानतनुवीचिनिमज्जनौघविध्वस्तपाप्ममुनिसिद्धमनुष्यवन्द्या ॥ 50
37.m: Worshipped by sages, accomplished beings, and mortals whose sins were destroyed by plunging into the mass of her slender waves that were showered / with the perfumes and flowers of worship applied to the self-manifest Siddha-liṅgas of Maheśvara established on her banks;

37.s:
bhogāpavargaparipūraṇakalpavallī bhogaikadānarasikāṃ surasiddhasindhum /
nyakkurvatī harapinākakalāvatīrṇā yadbhūṣayatyavirataṃ taṭinī vitastā // 51
37.d:
भोगापवर्गपरिपूरणकल्पवल्ली भोगैकदानरसिकां सुरसिद्धसिन्धुम् ।
न्यक्कुर्वती हरपिनाककलावतीर्णा यद्भूषयत्यविरतं तटिनी वितस्ता ॥ 51
37.m: A wish-granting vine fulfilling both enjoyment and liberation, disparaging the river of the gods and perfected beings which delights only in granting enjoyment, / descended from the tip of Śiva's bow: the river Vitastā, which ceaselessly adorns [that land].

37.s:
tasmin kuverapuracārisiṃtāṃśumaulisāṃmukhyadarśanavirūḍhapavitrabhāve /
vaitastarodhasi nivāsamamuṣya cakre rājā dvijasya parikalpitabhūrisaṃpat // 52
37.d:
तस्मिन् कुवेरपुरचारिसिंतांशुमौलिसांमुख्यदर्शनविरूढपवित्रभावे ।
वैतस्तरोधसि निवासममुष्य चक्रे राजा द्विजस्य परिकल्पितभूरिसंपत् ॥ 52
37.m: On the bank of that Vitastā, which was imbued with holiness by directly gazing upon the Moon-crested Lord who moves in the city of Kuvera, / the king provided ample wealth and settled this twice-born one.

37.s:
tasyānvaye mahati ko'pi varāhaguptanāmā babhūva bhagavān svayamantakāle /
gīrvāṇasindhulaharīkalitāgramūrdhā yasyākarot paramanugrahamāgraheṇa // 53
37.d:
तस्यान्वये महति कोऽपि वराहगुप्तनामा बभूव भगवान् स्वयमन्तकाले ।
गीर्वाणसिन्धुलहरीकलिताग्रमूर्धा यस्याकरोत् परमनुग्रहमाग्रहेण ॥ 53
37.m: In his great lineage there arose a venerable man named Varāhagupta, / upon whom at the time of death the Lord Himself, whose crown is adorned with the waves of the river of the gods, zealously bestowed the highest grace.

37.s:
tasyātmajaścukhalaketi jane prasiddhaścandrāvadātadhiṣaṇo narasiṃhaguptaḥ /
yaṃ sarvaśāstrarasamajjanaśubhracittaṃ māheśvarī paramalaṃkurute sma bhaktiḥ // 54
37.d:
तस्यात्मजश्चुखलकेति जने प्रसिद्धश्चन्द्रावदातधिषणो नरसिंहगुप्तः ।
यं सर्वशास्त्ररसमज्जनशुभ्रचित्तं माहेश्वरी परमलंकुरुते स्म भक्तिः ॥ 54
37.m: His son was Narasiṃhagupta, known among the people as Cukhalaka, whose intellect was pure as the moon; / whose mind was purified by plunging into the nectar of all the scriptures, and whom devotion to Maheśvara supremely adorned.

37.s:
tāruṇyasāgarataraṅgabharānapohya vairāgyapotamadhiruhya dṛḍhaṃ haṭhena /
yo bhaktirohaṇamavāpya maheśacintāratnairalaṃ dalayati sma bhavāpadastāḥ // 55
37.d:
तारुण्यसागरतरङ्गभरानपोह्य वैराग्यपोतमधिरुह्य दृढं हठेन ।
यो भक्तिरोहणमवाप्य महेशचिन्तारत्नैरलं दलयति स्म भवापदस्ताः ॥ 55
37.m: Who, having cast aside the surging waves of the ocean of youth and firmly mounted the boat of dispassion by main force, / reached the Mount Rohaṇa of devotion and utterly shattered the calamities of worldly existence with the wish-fulfilling gems of contemplation on Maheśvara.

37.s:
tasyātmajo'bhinavagupta iti prasiddhaḥ śrīcandracūḍacaraṇābjaparāgapūtaḥ /
mātā vyayūyujadamuṃ kila bālya eva daivaṃ hi bhāviparikarmaṇi saṃskaroti // 56
37.d:
तस्यात्मजोऽभिनवगुप्त इति प्रसिद्धः श्रीचन्द्रचूडचरणाब्जपरागपूतः ।
माता व्ययूयुजदमुं किल बाल्य एव दैवं हि भाविपरिकर्मणि संस्करोति ॥ 56
37.m: His son is known as Abhinavagupta, purified by the pollen of the lotus feet of the Moon-crested Lord; / his mother indeed left him while still in childhood, for destiny prepares one for future spiritual refinement.

37.s:
mātā paraṃ bandhuriti pravādaḥ snoho'tigāḍhīkurute hi pāśān /
tanmūlabandhe galite kilāsya manye sthitā jīvata eva muktiḥ // 57
37.d:
माता परं बन्धुरिति प्रवादः स्नोहोऽतिगाढीकुरुते हि पाशान् ।
तन्मूलबन्धे गलिते किलास्य मन्ये स्थिता जीवत एव मुक्तिः ॥ 57
37.m: The common saying is that a mother is the supreme relation, for affection makes bonds exceedingly tight; / when that root bond had slipped away, I think liberation in this very life became established for him.

37.s:
pitrā sa śabdagahane kṛtasaṃpraveśastarkārṇavormipṛṣatāmalapūtacittaḥ /
sāhityasāndrarasabhogaparo maheśabhaktyā svayaṃgrahaṇadurmadayā gṛhītaḥ // 58
37.d:
पित्रा स शब्दगहने कृतसंप्रवेशस्तर्कार्णवोर्मिपृषतामलपूतचित्तः ।
साहित्यसान्द्ररसभोगपरो महेशभक्त्या स्वयंग्रहणदुर्मदया गृहीतः ॥ 58
37.m: Introduced by his father into the dense forest of grammar, his mind made spotlessly pure by the spray from the waves of the ocean of logic, / dedicated to the enjoyment of the rich aesthetic savor of literature, he was seized by devotion to Maheśvara, which is intoxicated by seizing [one] of its own accord.

37.s:
sa tanmayībhūya na lokavartanīmajīgaṇat kāmapi kevalaṃ punaḥ /
tadīyasaṃbhogavivṛddhaye purā karoti dāsyaṃ guruveśmasu svayam // 59
37.d:
स तन्मयीभूय न लोकवर्तनीमजीगणत् कामपि केवलं पुनः ।
तदीयसंभोगविवृद्धये पुरा करोति दास्यं गुरुवेश्मसु स्वयम् ॥ 59
37.m: Becoming absorbed in that, he took no account whatsoever of worldly ways; / rather, simply to enhance the enjoyment of that, he formerly rendered service in the homes of the gurus with his own hands.

37.s:
ānandasaṃtatimahārṇavakarṇadhāraḥ saddaiśikairakavarātmajavāmanāthaḥ /
śrīnāthasaṃtatimahāmbaragharmakāntiḥ śrībhūtirājatanayaḥ svapitṛprasādaḥ // 60
37.d:
आनन्दसंततिमहार्णवकर्णधारः सद्दैशिकैरकवरात्मजवामनाथः ।
श्रीनाथसंततिमहाम्बरघर्मकान्तिः श्रीभूतिराजतनयः स्वपितृप्रसादः ॥ 60
37.m: Vāmanātha, the son of the excellent teacher Eraka, who was the helmsman on the vast ocean of the lineage of Ānanda; / the glorious son of Bhūtirāja, an ornament of light in the vast sky of the lineage of the glorious Nātha, having received the grace of his own father;

37.s:
traiyambakaprasarasāgaraśāyisomānandātmajotpalajalakṣmaṇaguptanāthaḥ /
turyākhyasaṃtatimahodadhipūrṇacandraḥ śrīsomataḥ sakalavitkila śaṃbhunāthaḥ // 61
37.d:
त्रैयम्बकप्रसरसागरशायिसोमानन्दात्मजोत्पलजलक्ष्मणगुप्तनाथः ।
तुर्याख्यसंततिमहोदधिपूर्णचन्द्रः श्रीसोमतः सकलवित्किल शंभुनाथः ॥ 61
37.m: Lakṣmaṇaguptanātha, son of Utpala who was born of Somānanda, resting on the ocean of the transmission of Traiyambaka; / the all-knowing Śambhunātha, the full moon to the great ocean of the lineage called the Fourth, [descended] from glorious Soma;

37.s:
śrīcandraśarmabhavabhaktivilāsayogānandābhinandaśivaśaktivicitranāthāḥ /
anye'pi dharmaśivavāmanakodbhaṭaśrībhūteśabhāskaramukhapramukhā mahāntaḥ // 62
37.d:
श्रीचन्द्रशर्मभवभक्तिविलासयोगानन्दाभिनन्दशिवशक्तिविचित्रनाथाः ।
अन्येऽपि धर्मशिववामनकोद्भटश्रीभूतेशभास्करमुखप्रमुखा महान्तः ॥ 62
37.m: The glorious Candraśarman, Bhavabhakti, Vilāsa, Yogānanda, Abhinanda, Śivaśakti, and Vicitranātha; / and other great ones, foremost among whom were Dharmaśiva, Vāmanaka, Udbhaṭa, the glorious Bhūteśa, and Bhāskara:

37.s:
ete sevārasaviracitānugrahāḥ śāstrasārapauḍhādeśaprakaṭasubhagaṃ svādhikāraṃ kilāsmai /
yat saṃprāduryadapi ca janānnaikṣatākṣetrabhūtān svātmārāmastadayamaniśaṃ tattvasevāraso'bhūt // 63
37.d:
एते सेवारसविरचितानुग्रहाः शास्त्रसारपौढादेशप्रकटसुभगं स्वाधिकारं किलास्मै ।
यत् संप्रादुर्यदपि च जनान्नैक्षताक्षेत्रभूतान् स्वात्मारामस्तदयमनिशं तत्त्वसेवारसोऽभूत् ॥ 63
37.m: Because these masters, whose grace was fashioned by the joy of devotion, truly transmitted to him their spiritual authority, made resplendent through the mature teaching that is the essence of scripture, / and because he did not see ordinary people as suitable recipients, this man, finding delight in his own self, ceaselessly experienced the savor of serving ultimate reality.

37.s:
so'nugrahītumatha śāṃbhavabhaktibhājaṃ svaṃ bhrātaramakhilaśāstravimarśapūrṇam /
yāvanmanaḥ praṇidadhāti manorathākhyaṃ tāvajjanaḥ katipayastamupāsasāda // 64
37.d:
सोऽनुग्रहीतुमथ शांभवभक्तिभाजं स्वं भ्रातरमखिलशास्त्रविमर्शपूर्णम् ।
यावन्मनः प्रणिदधाति मनोरथाख्यं तावज्जनः कतिपयस्तमुपाससाद ॥ 64
37.m: Then, as he turned his mind toward bestowing grace on his own brother named Manoratha, who was filled with reflective awareness of all scriptures and devoted to Śambhu, / a certain group of people approached him:

37.s:
śrīśaurisaṃjñatanayaḥ kila karṇanāmā yo yauvane viditaśāṃbhavatattvasāraḥ /
dehaṃ tyajan prathayati sma janasya satyaṃ yogacyutaṃ prati mahāmunikṛṣṇavākyam // 65
37.d:
श्रीशौरिसंज्ञतनयः किल कर्णनामा यो यौवने विदितशांभवतत्त्वसारः ।
देहं त्यजन् प्रथयति स्म जनस्य सत्यं योगच्युतं प्रति महामुनिकृष्णवाक्यम् ॥ 65
37.m: Namely, the son of the glorious Śauri, known as Karṇa, who in his youth came to know the essence of the reality of Śambhu, / and who, in casting off his body, proved true to the people the word of the great sage Kṛṣṇa concerning the one who has fallen from yoga;

37.s:
tadbālamitramatha mantrisutaḥ prasiddhaḥ śrīmandra ityakhilasāraguṇābhirāmaḥ /
lakṣmīsarasvati samaṃ yamalaṃcakāra sāpatnakaṃ tirayate subhagaprabhāvaḥ // 66
37.d:
तद्बालमित्रमथ मन्त्रिसुतः प्रसिद्धः श्रीमन्द्र इत्यखिलसारगुणाभिरामः ।
लक्ष्मीसरस्वति समं यमलंचकार सापत्नकं तिरयते सुभगप्रभावः ॥ 66
37.m: Then his childhood friend, the well-known minister's son the glorious Mandra, delightful with all essential virtues, / whom Fortune and Sarasvatī adorned together, his charming splendor setting aside their natural rivalry;

37.s:
anye pitṛvyatanayāḥ śivaśaktiśubhrāḥ kṣemotpalābhinavacakrakapadmaguptāḥ /
ye saṃpadaṃ tṛṇamamaṃsata śaṃbhusevāsaṃpūritaṃ svahṛdayaṃ hṛdi bhāvayantaḥ // 67
37.d:
अन्ये पितृव्यतनयाः शिवशक्तिशुभ्राः क्षेमोत्पलाभिनवचक्रकपद्मगुप्ताः ।
ये संपदं तृणममंसत शंभुसेवासंपूरितं स्वहृदयं हृदि भावयन्तः ॥ 67
37.m: Other sons of his paternal uncles, radiant with the power of Śiva—Kṣemagupta, Utpalagupta, Abhinavagupta, Cakragupta, and Padmagupta— / who considered worldly wealth a blade of grass, contemplating in their hearts their own heart filled with service to Śambhu;

37.s:
ṣaḍardhaśāstreṣu samastameva yenādhijagme vidhimaṇḍalādi /
sa rāmagupto guruśaṃbhuśāstrasevāvidhivyagrasamagramārgaḥ // 68
37.d:
षडर्धशास्त्रेषु समस्तमेव येनाधिजग्मे विधिमण्डलादि ।
स रामगुप्तो गुरुशंभुशास्त्रसेवाविधिव्यग्रसमग्रमार्गः ॥ 68
37.m: Rāmagupta, who mastered everything in the Trika scriptures, including the rules and the mandala, / his entire course fully engaged in the practice of serving the scriptures of the Guru and Śambhu;

37.s:
anyo'pi kaścana janaḥ śivaśaktipātasaṃpreraṇāparavaśasvakaśaktisārthaḥ /
abhyarthanāvimukhabhāvamaśikṣitena tenāpyanugrahapadaṃ kṛta eṣa vargaḥ // 69
37.d:
अन्योऽपि कश्चन जनः शिवशक्तिपातसंप्रेरणापरवशस्वकशक्तिसार्थः ।
अभ्यर्थनाविमुखभावमशिक्षितेन तेनाप्यनुग्रहपदं कृत एष वर्गः ॥ 69
37.m: And another group of people whose faculties were subordinated by the impulsion of Śiva's descent of power; / this circle, having learned no refusal of requests, was made a recipient of grace by him.

37.s:
ācāryamabhyarthayate sma gāḍhaṃ saṃpūrṇatantrādhigamāya samyak /
jāyeta daivānugṛhītabuddheḥ saṃpatprabandhaikarasaiva saṃpat // 70
37.d:
आचार्यमभ्यर्थयते स्म गाढं संपूर्णतन्त्राधिगमाय सम्यक् ।
जायेत दैवानुगृहीतबुद्धेः संपत्प्रबन्धैकरसैव संपत् ॥ 70
37.m: They fervently petitioned the master for a complete comprehension of the tantras; / for one whose intellect is graced by destiny, fortune yields a continuity of uninterrupted fortune alone.

37.s:
so'pyabhyupāgamadabhīpsitamasya yadvā svātodyameva hi ninartiṣato'vatīrṇam /
so'nugrahapravaṇa eva hi sadgurūṇāmājñāvaśena śubhasūtimahāṅkureṇa // 71
37.d:
सोऽप्यभ्युपागमदभीप्सितमस्य यद्वा स्वातोद्यमेव हि निनर्तिषतोऽवतीर्णम् ।
सोऽनुग्रहप्रवण एव हि सद्गुरूणामाज्ञावशेन शुभसूतिमहाङ्कुरेण ॥ 71
37.m: He too agreed to their desire, or rather, his own musical instrument descended for him who wished to dance; / for he was wholly inclined to bestow grace, by virtue of the command of his good gurus, through the great sprout of auspicious birth.

37.s:
vikṣiptabhāvaparihāramatho cikīrṣan mandraḥ svake puravare sthitimasya vavre /
ābālagopamapi yatra maheśvarasya dāsyaṃ janaścarati pīṭhanivāsakalpe // 72
37.d:
विक्षिप्तभावपरिहारमथो चिकीर्षन् मन्द्रः स्वके पुरवरे स्थितिमस्य वव्रे ।
आबालगोपमपि यत्र महेश्वरस्य दास्यं जनश्चरति पीठनिवासकल्पे ॥ 72
37.m: Then, desiring to remove distractions, Mandra requested his stay in his own excellent town, / which was like a dwelling in a sacred seat, where people down to children and cowherds perform service to Maheśvara.

37.s:
tasyābhavat kila pitṛvyavadhūrvidhātrā yā nirmame galitasaṃsṛticitracintā /
śītāṃśumaulicaraṇābjaparāgamātrabhūṣāvidhirvihitavatsalikocitākhyā // 73
37.d:
तस्याभवत् किल पितृव्यवधूर्विधात्रा या निर्ममे गलितसंसृतिचित्रचिन्ता ।
शीतांशुमौलिचरणाब्जपरागमात्रभूषाविधिर्विहितवत्सलिकोचिताख्या ॥ 73
37.m: There was indeed his paternal uncle's wife, whom the Creator made free from the manifold anxieties of worldly existence, / whose sole ornament was the pollen of the lotus feet of the Moon-crested Lord, and who was appropriately named Vatsalikā;

37.s:
mūrtā kṣameva karuṇeva gṛhītadehā dhāreva vigrahavatī śubhaśīlatāyāḥ /
vairāgyasāraparipākadaśeva pūrṇā tattvārtharatnarucirasthitirohaṇorvī // 74
37.d:
मूर्ता क्षमेव करुणेव गृहीतदेहा धारेव विग्रहवती शुभशीलतायाः ।
वैराग्यसारपरिपाकदशेव पूर्णा तत्त्वार्थरत्नरुचिरस्थितिरोहणोर्वी ॥ 74
37.m: Like forgiveness embodied, like compassion taking bodily form, like an incarnate stream of good conduct, / like the complete state of full maturity of the essence of dispassion, the Mount Rohaṇa for the radiant presence of the jewels of reality.

37.s:
bhrātāpi tasyāḥ śaśiśubhramaulerbhaktyā paraṃ pāvitacittavṛttiḥ /
sa śaurirātteśvaramantribhāvastatyāja yo bhūpatimantribhāvam // 75
37.d:
भ्रातापि तस्याः शशिशुभ्रमौलेर्भक्त्या परं पावितचित्तवृत्तिः ।
स शौरिरात्तेश्वरमन्त्रिभावस्तत्याज यो भूपतिमन्त्रिभावम् ॥ 75
37.m: Her brother too, his mind's activity supremely purified through devotion to the one whose crest is bright with the moon, / was Śauri, who, having assumed the status of counselor to the Lord, cast off his status as counselor to the king. // 75

37.s:
tasya snuṣā karṇavadhūrvidhūtasaṃsāravṛttiḥ sutamekameva /
yāsūta yogeśvaridattasaṃjñaṃ nāmānurūpasphuradarthatattvam // 76
37.d:
तस्य स्नुषा कर्णवधूर्विधूतसंसारवृत्तिः सुतमेकमेव ।
यासूत योगेश्वरिदत्तसंज्ञं नामानुरूपस्फुरदर्थतत्त्वम् ॥ 76
37.m: His daughter-in-law, the wife of Karṇa, whose worldly pursuits were shaken off, / gave birth to an only son named Yogeśvaridatta, the reality of whose nature shone forth in accordance with his name. // 76

37.s:
yāmagrage vayasi bhartṛviyogadīnāmanvagrahīt trinayanaḥ svayameva bhaktyā /
bhāviprabhāvarabhaseṣu janeṣvanarthaḥ satyaṃ samākṛṣati so'rthaparamparāṇām // 77
37.d:
यामग्रगे वयसि भर्तृवियोगदीनामन्वग्रहीत् त्रिनयनः स्वयमेव भक्त्या ।
भाविप्रभावरभसेषु जनेष्वनर्थः सत्यं समाकृषति सोऽर्थपरम्पराणाम् ॥ 77
37.m: Whom, wretched in her youth by separation from her husband, the Three-eyed Lord himself graced on account of her devotion; / truly, when persons are marked by the vehement energy of future spiritual power, adversity attracts a succession of treasures. // 77

37.s:
bhaktyullasatpulakatāṃ sphuṭamaṅgabhūṣāṃ śrīśaṃbhunāthanatimeva lalāṭikāṃ ca /
śaivaśrutiṃ śravaṇabhūṣaṇamapyavāpya saubhāgyamabhyadhikamudvahati sma yāntaḥ // 78
37.d:
भक्त्युल्लसत्पुलकतां स्फुटमङ्गभूषां श्रीशंभुनाथनतिमेव ललाटिकां च ।
शैवश्रुतिं श्रवणभूषणमप्यवाप्य सौभाग्यमभ्यधिकमुद्वहति स्म यान्तः ॥ 78
37.m: Having obtained the bristling of bodily hair dancing with devotion as an evident body ornament, bowing to illustrious Śambhunātha as her forehead jewel, / and Śaiva revelation as her ear ornament, she bore within her an extraordinary auspicious fortune. // 78

37.s:
ambābhidhānā kila sā guruṃ taṃ svaṃ bhrātaraṃ śaṃbhudṛśābhyapaśyat /
bhāviprabhāvojjvalabhavyabuddhiḥ sato'vajānāti na bandhubuddhyā // 79
37.d:
अम्बाभिधाना किल सा गुरुं तं स्वं भ्रातरं शंभुदृशाभ्यपश्यत् ।
भाविप्रभावोज्ज्वलभव्यबुद्धिः सतोऽवजानाति न बन्धुबुद्ध्या ॥ 79
37.m: Known indeed by the name Ambā, she beheld that brother of hers, the guru, with the gaze [that beholds] Śiva; / one whose noble intellect is radiant with future spiritual power does not disregard the virtuous thinking of them [merely] as kin. // 79

37.s:
bhrātā tadīyo'bhinavaśca nāmnā na kevalaṃ saccaritairapi svaiḥ /
pītena vijñānarasena yasya tatraiva tṛṣṇā vavṛdhe nikāmam // 80
37.d:
भ्राता तदीयोऽभिनवश्च नाम्ना न केवलं सच्चरितैरपि स्वैः ।
पीतेन विज्ञानरसेन यस्य तत्रैव तृष्णा ववृधे निकामम् ॥ 80
37.m: And her brother, Abhinava, was so named not only [by convention], but also because of his own noble deeds, / whose thirst for that very thing grew exceedingly through the nectar of experiential knowledge he had drunk. // 80

37.s:
so'nyaśca śāṃbhavamarīcicayapraṇaśyatsaṃkocahārdanalinīghaṭitojjvalaśrīḥ /
taṃ lumpakaḥ paricacāra samudyameṣu sādhuḥ samāvahati hanta karāvalambam // 81
37.d:
सोऽन्यश्च शांभवमरीचिचयप्रणश्यत्संकोचहार्दनलिनीघटितोज्ज्वलश्रीः ।
तं लुम्पकः परिचचार समुद्यमेषु साधुः समावहति हन्त करावलम्बम् ॥ 81
37.m: And that other one, Lumpaka, whose radiant splendor unfolded like the lotus of the heart shedding its contraction through the array of Śiva's rays, / served him in his undertakings; indeed, a good person extends a helping hand! // 81

37.s:
itthaṃ gṛhe vatsalikāvitīrṇe sthitaḥ samādhāya matiṃ bahūni /
pūrvaśrutānyākalayan svabuddhyā śāstrāṇi tebhyaḥ samavāpa sāram // 82
37.d:
इत्थं गृहे वत्सलिकावितीर्णे स्थितः समाधाय मतिं बहूनि ।
पूर्वश्रुतान्याकलयन् स्वबुद्ध्या शास्त्राणि तेभ्यः समवाप सारम् ॥ 82
37.m: Thus residing in the house bestowed by Vatsalikā, having collected his mind, / bringing to mind with his own intellect the many scriptures he had previously heard, he drew forth the essence from them. // 82

37.s:
sa tannibandhaṃ vidadhe mahārthaṃ yuktyāgamodīritatantratattvam /
ālokamāsādya yadīyameṣa lokaḥ sukhaṃ saṃcaritā kriyāsu // 83
37.d:
स तन्निबन्धं विदधे महार्थं युक्त्यागमोदीरिततन्त्रतत्त्वम् ।
आलोकमासाद्य यदीयमेष लोकः सुखं संचरिता क्रियासु ॥ 83
37.m: He composed this treatise of great import, the reality of whose Tantras is proclaimed by reasoning and scripture, / having gained the light of which, this world will move with ease in ritual actions. // 83

37.s:
santo'nugṛhṇīta kṛtiṃ tadīyāṃ hṛhṇīta pūrvaṃ vidhireṣa tāvat /
tato'pi gṛhṇātu bhavanmatiṃ sā sadyo'nugṛhṇātu ca tattvadṛṣṭyā // 84
37.d:
सन्तोऽनुगृह्णीत कृतिं तदीयां हृह्णीत पूर्वं विधिरेष तावत् ।
ततोऽपि गृह्णातु भवन्मतिं सा सद्योऽनुगृह्णातु च तत्त्वदृष्ट्या ॥ 84
37.m: O virtuous ones, favor his work, receive it first; this is the proper procedure. / Thereupon, may it seize your mind and immediately grace you with the vision of reality! // 84

37.s:
idamabhinavaguptaprombhitaṃ śāstrasāraṃ śiva niśamaya tāvat sarvataḥśrotratantraḥ /
tava kila nutireṣā sā hi tvadrūpacarcetyabhinavaparituṣṭo lokamātmīkuruṣva // 85
37.d:
इदमभिनवगुप्तप्रोम्भितं शास्त्रसारं शिव निशमय तावत् सर्वतःश्रोत्रतन्त्रः ।
तव किल नुतिरेषा सा हि त्वद्रूपचर्चेत्यभिनवपरितुष्टो लोकमात्मीकुरुष्व ॥ 85
37.m: O Śiva, you whose ear is independent everywhere, hear this essence of the scriptures woven by Abhinavagupta; / indeed, this is praise of you, for it is contemplation of your nature; thus, delighted anew, make the world your own! // 85
